subject: Pilot alignment: scope, success metrics, owners, and access checklist
messages:
From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sophie Tran <sophie.tran@bluefront.ai>, Ben Jacobs <ben.j@bluefront.ai>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwoodinference.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sun, 11 Oct 2026 16:10:00 -0700
Subject: Pilot alignment: scope, success metrics, owners, and access checklist

Hi Sophie / Ben —

Thanks again for the call earlier today. Quick recap from our side and proposed next steps so we’re all aligned before we kick off the pilot: 

Key pain points you shared
- Low-quality retrieval & hallucinations in domain-specific KB responses (esp. policy documents).
- Unpredictable token costs when running long-context prompts across many customer records.
- Need for auditable logs for compliance review.

Pilot goals (30-day sprint)
1) Reduce hallucination rate on knowledge queries by 40% (measured via the prompt eval set).
2) Achieve median token latency < 250ms for 1k-token contexts in our dedicated environment.
3) Deliver logs and retention config to satisfy your audit workflow.

Scope we propose
- Model: distil-open-12b (proof-of-concept), fallback to quantized 8-bit variant for burst tests.
- Workloads: 2 evaluation prompt sets (policy Q&A + customer summaries), 1000 sample docs for indexing.
- Integration: API-based calls; no schema changes on your side.

Ownership & roles
- Bluefront: Sophie (product lead) — prompt/labeling owners; Ben (infra) — access approvals and SSO.
- Redwood: Mateo — pilot PM and single point of contact; Vanessa — SRE/infra access; Grace — prompt-eval lead.

Immediate asks from Bluefront
- Provide SSO admin contact + expected account email domains for SAML setup.
- Share sample prompt set (10-20 canonical examples) and 250 sample docs for initial indexing.
- Confirm regulatory retention window for logs (we discussed 90 vs 365 days).

Attachments shared
- pilot_charter_bluefront_v1.pdf (charter + success metrics template)
- redwood_access_checklist.xlsx (accounts, firewall/IPs, SSO steps)
- prompt_evals_template.csv (format for labels)

Proposed timeline
- Week 0 (this week): access & SSO, inbox for log delivery, data sample upload.
- Week 1: baseline evals + prompt tuning.
- Week 2: dedicated infra provisioning & latency tuning.
- Week 3: validation run and handoff to your reviewers.

Can you confirm availability for a 30-minute kickoff on Tuesday, Oct 13 at 10:00 AM PT? If that works we’ll send the calendar invite and start the SSO setup flow.

Thanks — I’ll hold until I hear back on availability and SSO contact.

Best,
Mateo Alvarez
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
mateo.alvarez@redwoodinference.com | +1 (415) 555-0132

Date: Mon, 12 Oct 2026 09:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Pilot alignment: scope, success metrics, owners, and access checklist

Thanks Mateo — this is perfect and very clear. Quick answers from our side: 

- Tuesday Oct 13, 10:00 AM PT works for Sophie and me — we’ve blocked it.
- SSO admin is Ben (ben.j@bluefront.ai) — he’ll follow up with the SAML metadata and the list of domains.
- For retention, we need logs retained for 365 days for compliance, but we can start with a 90-day retention for the pilot if it simplifies the setup; we’ll want the option to enable 365 in prod.
- We’ll upload the first batch of 250 docs and a 15-example prompt set to the Drive folder by EOD Monday.

One procurement note: procurement@bluefront.ai asked whether you can share a short summary of data handling during the pilot (where tokens and logs are stored, who has access) so they can attach it to the PO.

Looking forward to the kickoff.

— Sophie
Head of Product, Bluefront AI
Sophie.Tran@bluefront.ai | +1 (617) 555-8821

Thanks Sophie — great. We’ll send the calendar invite in a moment. Attached is a short one-pager focused on data handling for procurement, plus the SSO onboarding doc. Quick answers here: 

- Pilot data & logs: stored in Redwood's dedicated environment for the pilot region (us-west-2). Access is restricted to the pilot team; full audit logs are available via the console and can be exported.
- Token handling: request/response tokens are ephemeral and not used to train any models. We include a sample log schema in the one-pager.
- Admin & access: Ben will be added to our SAML tenant; Vanessa (SRE) will coordinate the firewall/IP allowlist.

Next steps I’m owning this week
- Send calendar invite for 10/13 10:00 AM PT (INVITE SENT).
- Kick off SAML metadata exchange (Ben to provide).
- Provision a staging namespace and drop initial eval baseline by Oct 15.

Vanessa / Grace: can one of you pick up SSO provisioning and baseline evals respectively?

Thanks — Mateo
